A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TACLR and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B. The proprietary dataset can be matched across its renaming through identical taxonomy statistics and retained results.

before.justification: V2 reports original accuracy, inference-efficiency, ablation, and generalization experiments on Ecom-PAVI and WDC-PAVE in Tables 4–5 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds RAG comparisons in Tables 4–5 and a value-type subset evaluation in Table 6.

M1.justification: The shared encoder, taxonomy-aware contrastive loss, null-value thresholds, and top-1 prediction procedure remain unchanged. Faiss indexing and explicit input templates are newly documented implementation details; the added null-inclusive argmax restates the existing inference rule.

E1.justification: Ecom-PAVI is renamed Xianyu-PAVI, with unchanged Table 2 statistics. WDC-PAVE, its non-measurement evaluation, and the existing cross-category and cross-value scenarios remain. The new value-type analysis partitions already represented test data.

E2.justification: V3 adds Llama3.1 (RAG) and Qwen2.5 (RAG) to accuracy comparisons on both datasets and to the efficiency comparison in Tables 4–5. These BGE-based retrieval-augmented generators introduce a materially different comparison strategy while retaining all earlier comparators.

E3.justification: V3 introduces top-5 training-example retrieval for RAG and ground-truth-type partitioning for the new subset evaluation. Section 4.1 describes random sampling and drops v2's assurance about different time periods; unchanged Table 2 counts do not establish actual resplitting or rerunning.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Table 6 add a focused comparison of TACLR and fine-tuned LLMs on normalized versus pooled unnormalized/implicit values. The existing negative-sampling, threshold, prompt, and OOD analyses in Figures 4–5 retain their results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or statistical tests. Tables and plots report point estimates in both versions.

E6.justification: New RAG accuracy and efficiency results, together with Table 6's value-type scores, substantially extend the reported evidence. On WDC-PAVE, RAG F1 is 77.2 for Llama3.1 and 74.2 for Qwen2.5; their F1 Excl. scores are 80.1 and 78.3 against TACLR's retained 80.3. All pre-existing numerical entries in Tables 4–5 and Figures 4–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical task formulation, contrastive objective, and threshold decision rule are retained. Section 3.4's added argmax over candidates including null is presented as an equivalent expression, without a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about retrieval-based PAVI, implicit and OOD values, normalized outputs, scalability, and deployment. Naming Xianyu and announcing code release do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly discusses ongoing taxonomy maintenance and measurement-reasoning limitations, alongside the retained multimodal limitation. It also adds explanations involving classification-label sparsity, limited supervision on WDC-PAVE, and RAG's usefulness there. These provide additional qualifications within the existing interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies LoRA training settings for the already reported fine-tuned baselines, clarifies BERT-CLS's backbone and null prompts, and supplies code-release information. Sections 3–4 add exact item formatting, Faiss indexing, RAG construction, and annotation procedures. This materially improves implementation disclosure, although v2's maximum-feasible-batch rule for efficiency testing is omitted.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for LoRA, BGE, MoCo, product retrieval, and attribute mining. Section 2.1 replaces the multi-pass QA efficiency argument with an annotation-cost argument. The overall positioning against extraction, classification, and generation methods remains intact.

P1.justification: V3 updates dataset, platform, and affiliation names; clarifies unnormalized versus implicit values; and revises passages in the methods, results, and appendices. Section 3.2 gains descriptive subheadings, while the original section sequence and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 6, expands Tables 4–5 with RAG rows, and adjusts Table 4's grouping and rules. Several displays move with text reflow and captions are revised. The five existing figures retain their substantive visual content and the two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: The added RAG comparisons, previously missing LLM implementation details, and clearer applicability limits provide a limited net improvement in evaluation and reproducibility. The new robustness evidence needs clarification: Table 6's Llama3.1 subset F1 scores of 83.2 and 79.4 are not reconciled with its retained overall fine-tuned F1 of 84.7. The split-count discrepancy between Section 4.1 and Table 2 also persists, and removal of the efficiency batch-size rule weakens that disclosure.
